features.title: Union selected and generated Semgrep configs
features.user_visible_behavior: asdd audit / verify_architecture_rules run the project's .semgrep/ rule sets (architecture, standards, ...) plus rules generated from the specs' boundary tables. tech.md languages named in prose next to backticks are detected (previously none were, so no spec rule was ever generated here).

features.title: Analysis dashboard: mode title and Generate rules button
features.user_visible_behavior: The analysis dashboard heading names the mode (Security / Architecture / Standards), the rule-set selector offers Security, and a header button asks the agent to write rules for the mode's set: with existing rules it extends them (they keep running) and re-runs the same analyze tool. In security mode the button is hidden when the repo already has its own .semgrep/security/ set.
verification: cd tools/spec-drift && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && node --import tsx --test 'src/**/*.spec.ts' 'ui/**/*.spec.ts' && node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 test/*.e2e-spec.ts
features.evidence: typecheck, lint, build OK; unit 292 pass (incl. rules-prompt.spec.ts); e2e 145 pass (node v22.23.3); re-verified after hiding Generate security rules when .semgrep/security/ exists

features.title: Project-accurate .semgrep rule sets
features.user_visible_behavior: The repo's .semgrep/ architecture, standards and security sets scan this codebase with 0 false positives: built-in pack fixtures excluded, dom-xss limited to raw values, truncated-hash ids allowed, Python rules dropped; hook stdin streams, vendored-file exits and TypeScript servers are covered.
